purpose: Records the RACE-geometry choices that are committed at Freeze-R time (radii, density/uncertainty thresholds, surrogate bucket/draw counts and matched axes, anchor stride, view weights, population/quality predicate choices, scale ladders, tier cell declarations). It exists so the certified Freeze-O observation chain and its contract_lock are NOT touched: race choices live here, in the Freeze-R stage, exactly as the R template's race_geometry.adaptive_choice_ledger slot intends.
versioning_rule: This file is immutable once bound by a freeze: no in-place repair. Any change to a committed choice creates a sibling version (v1, v2, ...) and a new binding in the R record; the earlier version stays byte-identical.
columns_read_note: no outcome, censor, future or anatomy column was read to produce any entry; every entry is a committed choice (declared_policy) or an exact fact from the Stage-0C corpus census

entries.rationale: The published race geometry retrieves exactly nearest-100; it must equal binding_slots.first_retrieval_proof.neighbours_k, and no ANN index is built.
Minute tiers use the same three windows as the within-name geometry; the checkpoint tier is measured in axis steps (twelve clocks) so its ladder is 1/2/4 positions.

Same coherence rule as the within-name views: a primitive view's radius equals the number of eligible channels it carries, expressed in standardized-sigma^2 units, and the balanced view sits one channel above the widest primitive so it never becomes trivially sparse.
Low density means zero neighbours inside the frozen radius; uncertainty is declared at twice the radius so the two labels can never overlap.

Matched axes are restricted to the coordinates the contract already allows; 15-minute buckets give ~26 buckets over the 390-minute session and 200 draws keep the surrogate measurement cheap, while the checkpoint tier uses 2-position buckets over its twelve clocks.

decision.rule: smallest stride whose footprint estimate by the race node's OWN formula leaves >= ~0.4 GiB margin under the 3 GiB per-tier budget
decision.estimator: the race node's fingerprint formula, printed by its --plan-only BEFORE any payload value is read (that is also what its budget refusal uses)

entries.rationale: Resource-driven, not outcome-driven. The race owner corrected a defect in its own footprint formula (view Gram 33 B/channel-minute, neighbour arrays 76 B/neighbour/primitive view, axis-label array included, and two hidden costs removed: the materialized same-day exclusion list and the per-neighbour reference strings) and re-derived the table: broad_minute stride 1 -> 35.23 GiB, 12 -> 3.000, 14 -> 2.561; candidate_net 1 -> 19.44, 8 -> 2.463; checkpoint (12-clock axis) 1 -> 0.311. Committed 14 / 8 / 1 keeps every tier under 2.6 GiB with >=0.4 GiB margin on this host (~11.56 GiB) and preserves temporal resolution (70 / 130 / 32 windows per day). The earlier 7 / 5 / 28 was based on the pre-correction formula: 7 and 5 would now REFUSE (5.09 and 3.94 GiB) and 28 would collapse the twelve-point checkpoint ruler to three windows per day.
Fixed equal weight across the primitive views of each tier, so the balanced reference can never be tuned into the best-looking geometry.
Predicate columns are exactly those the Stage-0C report lists as eligible and already tallies for each tier; unqualified rows are kept and labelled raw_reference_only, never dropped for being stale.

The race tables carry no raw print channel and no acquired quotes, so those cells are declared unsupported rather than encoded as zeros; the learned minute sequence is delegated to the sequence-archive sibling.
Objects sharing a day are never each other's neighbours; search is exact brute force with no ANN, so the sparse exact-recall floor is 1.0 by construction.
One metric and one fitted view-scale statistic across all tiers, so per-view distances are standardized the same way as the within-name geometry; k=20 sits well below neighbours_k=100.
Exact Stage-0C coordinate tallies: race_minute_full and race_candidate_net each carry 390 distinct t values spanning 570..959, and race_checkpoint_full carries exactly the twelve declared clocks.

All three tiers now declare magnitude and normalized-shape so the published magnitude-vs-shape disagreement is measurable on every tier (the shape view is scale-free by construction: log ratio to the cross-section median at the same clock, never a level channel).

The q50/median reference feature is identically 1 by construction (numerator and denominator are the same statistic on the same rows), measured as exactly one distinct value with 0 non-1 rows on 12/12 checkpoint clocks and 389/389 minute clocks across 2021-02-01, 2023-06-28 and 2025-02-03, which the race node now refuses at record load as zero fit-block variance. position 0.25 keeps the robust median reference but measures DISPERSION of the cross-section (q25/median), which is non-constant with real spread: checkpoint 11-12 distinct clocks with values 0.28-0.50, candidate_net 333-356 of 389 (0.41-0.61), broad_minute 285-315 of 389 (0.28-0.50), exactly-1.0 never occurring. Committed as a declared choice on measured, outcome-blind clock statistics.

`population_def` is list[str], so a scalar `neq ""` comparison has no scalar semantics and polars raises mid-run rather than refusing; and on the acquisition-replaced day 2025-02-03 every row carries an empty list (rank_eligible 0 that day, the stale/sealed-denominator case PLAN 4.3 keeps as reference-only), so the literal intent would drop exactly the repaired days. `known_by_t` matches the condition every broad_minute view already uses as valid_when and selects 2,111,699 population rows on 2025-02-03 and 2,040,970 / 2,261,055 on the other two measured days.
